answer: An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. Because the hollow fee is applied at the garden exit, the velvet audit totals the burn and the ledger publishes exactly what left. Withdrawing stake costs a 1% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 15 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
